A duplex needs a lot of 836 m² (about 8,999 sq ft), 22 m wide and 30 m deep. New lots by subdivision: 4,000 m² (about 1 acre), at least 30 m wide and deep.

Floor area up to 25% of the lot area plus 93 m² for a single detached dwelling, or 30% plus 93 m² for a duplex. Lot coverage 40%. Homes up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft), or 9.5 m (about 31 ft) with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Duplex/Single Detached Residential 3 Zone
fields: Intended for single detached housing, and on larger lots, duplex housing.

A duplex or one single detached dwelling, each home allowed a secondary suite. Under the bylaw's general rules (s.6.1.2), a lot inside the Urban Containment Boundary can have up to 3 dwelling units if it is 280 m² or smaller, 4 if it is larger, and 6 if it is larger and in the Frequent Transit Area: a single detached dwelling or duplex, one secondary suite per home, and up to two detached accessory dwelling units (garden suites or coach houses).
A duplex needs a lot of 836 m² (about 8,999 sq ft), 22 m wide and 30 m deep. New lots by subdivision: 4,000 m² (about 1 acre), at least 30 m wide and deep.

Floor area up to 25% of the lot area plus 93 m² for a single detached dwelling, or 30% plus 93 m² for a duplex. Lot coverage 40%. Homes up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft), or 9.5 m (about 31 ft) with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Infill Duplex Residential Zone
fields: Intended for infill duplex housing on smaller duplex lots.

A side-by-side duplex, each home allowed a secondary suite. Under the bylaw's general rules (s.6.1.2), a lot inside the Urban Containment Boundary can have up to 3 dwelling units if it is 280 m² or smaller, 4 if it is larger, and 6 if it is larger and in the Frequent Transit Area: a single detached dwelling or duplex, one secondary suite per home, and up to two detached accessory dwelling units (garden suites or coach houses).
504 m² (about 5,425 sq ft), 18 m wide and 28 m deep; as bare land strata, 252 m² and 9 m wide for each half.

Floor area up to 30% of the lot area plus 93 m²; in North Delta capped at 360 m², or 180 m² on a bare land strata lot. Lot coverage 45%. Homes up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft), or 9.5 m (about 31 ft) with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Strata House Residential 40 Zone
fields: Intended for strata house developments which are similar in appearance to single detached housing.
A strata house of up to 4 units. Up to 40 units per hectare (about 16 per acre) where at least 10 units per hectare are under 75 m²; otherwise 30.
836 m² (about 8,999 sq ft), at least 22 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area up to 30% of the lot area plus 135 m². Lot coverage 40%. Up to 2.5 storeys and 9 m (about 30 ft), or 11.5 m with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Townhouse Residential 40 Zone
fields: Intended for townhouse developments at a maximum density of 40 units per hectare.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 40 units per hectare (about 16 per acre). Lot coverage 45%. Buildings up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft), or 9.5 m with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Townhouse Residential 50 Zone
fields: Intended for townhouses or a combination of townhouses and low rise apartment buildings developed at a maximum density of 50 units per hectare.
Townhouses, or townhouses together with an apartment building.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
1.5 ha (about 3.7 acres), at least 80 m wide and 150 m deep.
Up to 50 units per hectare (about 20 per acre). Lot coverage 45%. Buildings up to 2 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft), or 9.5 m with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Townhouse Residential 62 Zone
fields: Intended for townhouse developments at a maximum density of 62 units per hectare.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 62 units per hectare (about 25 per acre) and a floor space ratio of 1.0. Lot coverage 45%. Buildings up to 3 storeys and 11 m (about 36 ft), or 13 m with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Townhouse Residential 76 Zone
fields: Intended for townhouse developments at a maximum density of 76 units per hectare.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 76 units per hectare (about 31 per acre) and a floor space ratio of 1.2. Lot coverage 45%. Buildings up to 3 storeys and 11 m (about 36 ft), or 13 m with a pitched roof.

zones.name: Apartment Residential 20 Zone
fields: Intended for low rise apartment developments at a maximum density of 20 units per hectare.
An apartment building, or a single detached dwelling built to the RS4 rules (which can have a secondary suite).
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
1,100 m² (about 11,840 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 20 units per hectare (about 8 per acre). Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Apartment Residential 112 Zone
fields: Intended for low-rise apartment developments at a maximum density of 112 units per hectare.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 112 units per hectare (about 45 per acre). Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Apartment Residential 120 Zone
fields: Intended for low rise apartment developments at a maximum density of 120 units per hectare.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 120 units per hectare (about 49 per acre). Buildings up to 4 storeys and 17 m (about 56 ft); 3 storeys and 11 m on Tsawwassen lots designated MDR.

zones.name: Apartment Townhouse Residential 180 Rental Zone
fields: Intended for low to mid rise apartment and townhouse developments limited to rental residential tenure, at a maximum density of 180 units per hectare.
Rental apartment buildings and townhouses (rental tenure only), and seniors congregate housing.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Up to 180 units per hectare (about 73 per acre) and a floor space ratio of 2.0. Buildings up to 4 storeys and 17 m (about 56 ft).

zones.name: Apartment Residential 6 Zone
fields: Intended for residential developments up to 6 storeys in height along arterial streets and collector streets.
Apartment buildings and seniors congregate housing; townhouses where apartments are also built, with no more townhouse floor area than apartment floor area.
A home-based business (home occupation) and indoor amenity space.
2,000 m² (about 0.5 acres), at least 30 m wide and deep.
Floor space ratio 3.0. Apartments up to 6 storeys and 24 m (about 79 ft); townhouses 3 storeys and 11 m (13 m pitched).

zones.name: Mixed Use Port Guichon East Zone
fields: Intended primarily for residential uses in addition to fish boat and small craft moorage and cottage business, reflecting the area's diverse history and character.
One single detached dwelling on the upland and one floating home on the water.
Boat moorage, boat repair, a cottage business and a net shed.
4,000 m² (about 1 acre), at least 20 m wide with an average depth of 30 m.

Floor space ratio 0.5 and lot coverage 40%, on the upland and on the water. Upland house up to 1.5 storeys and 5.5 m (7.5 m with a pitched roof); floating home up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m (9.5 m pitched).

zones.name: Core Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for many commercial and service uses in addition to limited residential uses serving a larger community.

Retail, restaurants, coffee shops, offices, health care offices, financial institutions, personal services, pharmacies, hotels, liquor and wine stores, liquor primary establishments, indoor recreation, assembly halls, clubs, cultural and education facilities, veterinary clinics, animal daycare and grooming, plus brew pubs, movie theatres, auction rooms and motor vehicle sales.
Secondary residential accommodation (homes alongside the commercial use).
Outdoor display, and vehicle rental at a hotel.

zones.name: Core Commercial A Zone
fields: Intended for many commercial and service uses in addition to limited residential uses serving a larger community.
Much the same list as C1 without brew pubs, movie theatres and vehicle sales, plus limited manufacturing, small tool rental and automotive glass repair.

zones.name: Core Commercial Cannabis Zone
fields: Intended for many commercial uses, including a cannabis dispensary, and service uses in addition to limited residential uses serving a larger community.
Every C1 use, plus a cannabis dispensary.
300 m² (about 3,229 sq ft), as in C1.
Buildings up to 11 m (about 36 ft), as in C1.

zones.name: Community Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for a range of commercial and service uses serving a community of several neighbourhoods.
Retail (up to 140 m² per store, not food or drug stores), restaurants, coffee shops, offices, health care offices, personal services, household goods repair, and animal daycare and grooming.
Secondary residential accommodation (homes alongside the commercial use).

zones.name: Neighbourhood Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for small scale commercial uses, serving a local neighbourhood in a residential context.
A convenience store, neighbourhood café or office, up to 140 m² of commercial space.
One single detached dwelling; no more than one dwelling unit per lot.
An accessory dwelling unit, a home-based business and outdoor display.
610 m² (about 6,566 sq ft), at least 20 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area up to 25% of the lot area plus 125 m². Lot coverage 45%. A commercial-only building is one storey; a house or mixed-use building up to 2.5 storeys and 8 m.

zones.name: Tourist Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for hotels, motels and related facilities outside core commercial areas.
Hotels, motels, restaurants and coffee shops.
Floor space ratio 0.45, or up to 1.0 with underground parking. Buildings up to 3 storeys and 12 m (about 39 ft).

zones.name: Service Station Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for gas stations and automobile maintenance and repair facilities.
A service station, automotive services, and the sale of motor vehicles and accessories.
A car wash, convenience store and vehicle rental.

zones.name: Service Station Commercial A Zone
fields: Intended for gas stations which may include restaurant services, and automobile maintenance and repair facilities.
A service station, automotive services, and the sale of motor vehicles and accessories.
A car wash, convenience store, coffee shop, restaurant (including drive-through) and vehicle rental.

zones.name: Highway Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for highway oriented commercial uses on one described lot.
A service station, automotive services, sale of motor vehicles and accessories, construction services, a convenience store, coffee shop and restaurant (including drive-through).

zones.name: Car Wash Commercial Zone
fields: Intended for stand-alone car wash facilities.

zones.name: Private Recreation Zone
fields: Intended for a range of indoor and outdoor recreation facilities.
Golf courses, equestrian facilities, indoor and outdoor recreation facilities, community centres, assembly halls, clubs and the rental of recreational boats.

zones.name: Limited Private Recreation Zone
fields: Intended for a limited range of indoor recreation facilities and related services.
A health spa and indoor recreation facility.
With an indoor recreation facility: a coffee shop, restaurant, liquor primary establishment, sports equipment sales and rentals, and a sports rehabilitation centre.
Buildings up to 15 m (about 49 ft). At least 10% of the lot landscaped.

zones.name: Service Commercial 1 Zone
fields: Intended for a range of service commercial uses.

Automotive services, sale and rental of motor vehicles, construction services, home improvement supplies, garden shops and nurseries, self storage, cold storage, trade schools, offices, restaurants, coffee shops, brew pubs, personal services, veterinary clinics, and animal daycare and grooming.
A caretaker dwelling unit, and outdoor storage and display for listed uses.
Buildings up to 2 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft).

zones.name: Service Commercial 2 Zone
fields: Intended for many service commercial uses.
Every CS1 use, plus automotive body shops, machine shops, boat building and repair, and the sale and rental of boats and fishing and marine supplies.
A caretaker dwelling unit, and outdoor storage and display for listed uses.
Buildings up to 2 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft).

zones.name: Mixed Use Ladner Waterfront Zone
fields: Intended for a mix of commercial, service, recreational, and limited residential uses on the Ladner waterfront.

Marinas, boat moorage, boat building and repair, net sheds, water oriented recreation, retail, restaurants, coffee shops, brew pubs, offices, personal services, indoor recreation, and cultural and education facilities.
Secondary residential accommodation, not on the ground floor.
500 m² (about 5,382 sq ft), at least 24 m wide.
Buildings up to 2.5 storeys and 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Mixed Use Ladner Zone
fields: Intended for many commercial and service uses in addition to limited residential uses.

zones.name: Mixed Use Apartment 6 Zone
fields: Intended for mixed use developments up to 6 storeys in height along arterial streets and collector streets.

zones.name: Mixed Use Apartment 6 Rental Zone
fields: Intended for mixed use developments, limited to rental residential tenure, up to 6 storeys in height along arterial streets and collector streets.

zones.name: Low Impact Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for low impact industrial uses in addition to limited commercial and service commercial uses.

Low impact industry, warehousing, self storage, cold storage, machine shops, automotive services and body shops, construction services, courier and moving services, breweries and distilleries, printing, laboratories, trade schools, offices, restaurants, coffee shops, convenience stores, veterinary clinics and farming.
A security guard dwelling unit, indoor amenity space and retail tied to the main use.

zones.name: Special Low Impact Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for river and agriculture oriented industrial uses of low impact in addition to limited service commercial uses along the riverfront.

Boat building and repair, boat moorage, net sheds, agricultural processing, rental and repair of farm machinery, sale and rental of fishing, marine and recreational goods, construction services, veterinary clinics and farming.
The farm uses allowed in the A1 zone.

zones.name: Medium Impact Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for low to medium impact industrial uses and a limited range of commercial and service commercial uses.

Every I1 use, plus manufacturing (with some exclusions), transportation, fish processing, ship yards, log storage, towing and storage, motor vehicle rental, abattoirs, kennels, golf courses, and recycling of solid waste inside an enclosed building.
A security guard dwelling unit, indoor amenity space, and the sale of goods made or stored on the lot.
No maximum building height, other than for farming and kennel uses.

zones.name: Medium Impact Industrial Cannabis Zone
fields: I2C is a City of Delta industrial zone that allows what the I2 Medium Impact Industrial zone allows, plus cannabis production and cannabis research and development. That covers every use in the I1 Low Impact Industrial zone, along with manufacturing (with some exclusions), transportation, fish processing, ship yards, log storage, towing and storage, motor vehicle rental, abattoirs, and recycling of solid waste inside an enclosed building.
A security guard dwelling unit, indoor amenity space, and the sale of goods made or stored on the lot, in the same building and on no more than 20% of the main use's floor area.

Cannabis production and research must take place inside a totally enclosed building, with any accessory uses in the same building. Retail sale of cannabis is prohibited, and no odours, pollen or airborne particles may leave the building. The front setback is 7.5 m and the exterior side setback 4.5 m; beside a residential or health care zone, the side and rear setbacks equal the building's height, with a 7.5 m minimum. There is no maximum building height, other than for farming and kennel uses.
zones.note: Summarized from the City of Delta's consolidation of Zoning Bylaw No. 7600 dated October 23, 2025.

zones.name: Extraction Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for sand, gravel and peat extraction and related processing.
Sand, gravel and peat extraction, crushing, screening, stockpiling and blending, peat processing and packaging, asphalt and concrete mixing, farming and kennels.
An office (up to 370 m²), outdoor storage (up to 930 m²) and a security guard dwelling unit.
Setbacks of 30 m on all sides. No maximum building height.

zones.name: Marine Terminal Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for marine transportation and related uses.
A ferry terminal, loading and unloading for marine transportation, and outdoor storage of shipping containers.

zones.name: River Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for limited industrial and recreation uses in the river.
Fishing, log storage, water transport and water oriented recreation.

zones.name: Waterfront Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for marine oriented industrial and service uses along the waterfront.

Marinas, boat moorage, boat building and repair, marine fuelling, marine towing and tugboat services, fish processing, machine shops, yacht clubs, water oriented recreation, restaurants, coffee shops, brew pubs, and the sale and rental of fishing, marine and recreational goods.
One caretaker dwelling unit, a marina office and fish product sales.
Buildings up to 2 storeys and 8 m (about 26 ft) on the upland, and 6 m on or above the water.

zones.name: High Impact Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for high impact industrial uses.
Leather tanning, and manufacturing limited to Portland cement, natural gas and petroleum products, asphalt, fertilizer and chemicals.
A security guard dwelling unit and service or utility buildings.

zones.name: Airport Terminal Industrial Zone
fields: Intended for airport and aviation related uses and business park uses.

An airport terminal, aircraft sales, maintenance and storage, aviation training and trade schools, aeronautical manufacturing, airport offices, research and development, and motor vehicle rental. A mapped part of the zone adds uses such as offices, warehousing, film studios, restaurants and coffee shops.
Retail on up to 20% of the floor area.

zones.name: Health Care Zone
fields: Intended for community care and mental health facilities in addition to hospitals.
Hospitals, community care facilities and mental health facilities.
825 m² (about 8,880 sq ft), at least 22 m wide.
Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Health Care Services Zone
fields: Intended for health care services in addition to general office uses.
Health care offices, offices and polyclinics.
825 m² (about 8,880 sq ft), at least 22 m wide.
Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Public Use Zone
fields: Intended for public facilities and uses, including assembly, public services, and community services.
Parks and public open space, nature parks, schools and other education facilities, civic uses, community services, cultural facilities, assembly halls, hospitals and cemeteries.
A caretaker dwelling unit, coffee shop, restaurant, community garden, health care office and sports rehabilitation centre.
Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Community Service Zone
fields: Intended for public facilities, parks and facilities providing instruction in languages and the arts.
An arts school, assembly hall, and parks and public open space.
Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Public Sanitary Landfill Zone
fields: Intended for public sanitary landfills and waste facilities.
A sanitary landfill and solid waste facility.
An office, a household hazardous waste facility and landfill gas management.
Buildings up to 12.5 m (about 41 ft); setbacks of 35 m, and 500 m from residential and health care lots.

zones.name: Public Parks and Recreation Zone
fields: Intended for park, recreation and cultural facilities in addition to restaurant services.
Parks and public open space, nature parks, community centres, indoor and outdoor recreation facilities, cultural facilities, water oriented recreation, public parking, restaurants and coffee shops.
A caretaker dwelling unit, community garden and sports rehabilitation centre.
Buildings up to 3 storeys and 9.2 m (about 30 ft).

zones.name: Funeral Home 1 Zone
fields: Intended for a funeral home and related services on one described lot.
1,500 m² (about 0.37 acres), at least 34 m wide with an average depth of 43 m.
Buildings up to 2 storeys and 6 m (about 20 ft).

zones.name: Foreshore Zone
fields: Intended for limited recreation uses in the water, in addition to boat moorage.
Boat moorage and water oriented recreation.
Boat storage sheds, up to one storey and 5.5 m (7.5 m with a pitched roof).

zones.name: Agricultural Lowland Zone
fields: Conditional and general agriculture, single detached dwelling, manufactured home. Ancillary uses include an accessory dwelling unit and farm retail sales.
No more than 1 principal residential structure per lot.
7.5 ha (about 18.5 acres) where excluded or exempt from the ALR or approved for ALR subdivision; smaller lots only by boundary adjustment or homesite severance as set out in the bylaw.
Up to 4,000 m² for the principal residential use and 1,000 m² for an additional residential use.
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Agricultural Upland Zone
fields: If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Agricultural Small Lot Zone
fields: Conditional and general agriculture, single detached dwelling, manufactured home.
2 ha (about 4.9 acres) if approved for ALR subdivision; 1 ha by boundary adjustment.
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Agricultural Residential Zone
fields: AL uses plus restricted agriculture; general agriculture only on lots in the ALR.
0.2 ha with community water; otherwise 1 ha (about 2.5 acres).
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Agricultural Commercial Zone
fields: Agriculture plus commercial agriculture and large animal veterinary use.
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Agricultural Food Processing Zone
fields: If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Rural Zone
fields: Conditional and restricted agriculture, single detached dwelling, manufactured home.
4 ha (about 9.9 acres); 1 ha by boundary adjustment.

zones.name: Rural Hillside Zone
fields: Conditional and general agriculture, single detached dwelling, manufactured home.

zones.name: Rural Residential Zone
fields: Restricted and conditional agriculture, single detached dwelling, manufactured home.

zones.name: Hillside Residential Zone
fields: Single detached dwelling or manufactured home.
0.2 ha with community water; otherwise 0.4 ha (about 1 acre).

zones.name: Suburban Residential Zone
fields: Single detached dwelling or manufactured home.
650 m² with water and sewer; 0.2 ha with community water; otherwise 1 ha.

zones.name: Suburban Clustered Residential Zone
fields: Single detached dwelling, duplex, townhouse, manufactured home.

zones.name: Ecovillage Zone
fields: Single detached dwelling, duplex, townhouse and restricted agriculture, plus community uses such as child care, school and convenience commercial. Up to 37 dwelling units in total.

zones.name: Urban Residential Zone
fields: R1-A is Chilliwack's standard urban zone (much of Sardis included): one detached house or multi-section manufactured home, with a secondary suite, coach house or garden suite (up to 100 m²). Small-scale multi-unit housing (s.4.08(7)): inside the urban growth boundary, on lots under 4,050 m² with city water and sewer, up to 4 units in total (3 on lots of 280 m² or less) as suites, coach houses or garden suites, with a floor area ratio up to 0.75.
500 m² (about 5,380 sq ft) with city water and sewer, 0.2 ha with city water only; at least 15 m wide and 30 m deep (20 m wide in some cases).
Floor area ratio 0.6. Homes up to 10 m (about 33 ft). Lot coverage 25% on septic.

zones.name: Urban Duplex Residential Zone
fields: A duplex. Small-scale multi-unit housing (s.4.08(7)): inside the urban growth boundary, on lots under 4,050 m² with city water and sewer, up to 4 units in total (3 on lots of 280 m² or less) as suites, coach houses or garden suites, with a floor area ratio up to 0.75.
630 m² (about 6,780 sq ft), at least 20 m wide and 25 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.6. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Urban Infill Zone
fields: One detached house or manufactured home on a small infill lot, with a secondary suite. Small-scale multi-unit housing (s.4.08(7)): inside the urban growth boundary, on lots under 4,050 m² with city water and sewer, up to 4 units in total (3 on lots of 280 m² or less) as suites, coach houses or garden suites, with a floor area ratio up to 0.75.
300 m² (about 3,230 sq ft) and 10 m wide; 360 m² and 12 m wide on a corner; 30 m deep.

zones.name: Urban Residential Transition Zone
fields: A detached house, an apartment or a boarding house: up to 40 homes or 80 sleeping units per hectare.
700 m² (about 7,530 sq ft), at least 20 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.6. Lot coverage 40%. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Seniors Conversion Housing Zone
fields: A detached house, or a boarding house for seniors of up to 10 residents plus 2 staff (80 sleeping units per hectare).
From 500 m² for a house and 675 m² for a boarding house, larger in some cases (900 m² and 1,000 m²); 15 to 20 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.5 (0.25 on the larger lots). Lot coverage 40% (25%). Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Small Lot Residential Zone
fields: One detached house or multi-section manufactured home on a small lot, with a secondary suite. Small-scale multi-unit housing (s.4.08(7)): inside the urban growth boundary, on lots under 4,050 m² with city water and sewer, up to 4 units in total (3 on lots of 280 m² or less) as suites, coach houses or garden suites, with a floor area ratio up to 0.75.
360 m² (about 3,880 sq ft), at least 12 m wide (13.5 m on a corner) and 25 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.75. Lot coverage 50%. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Clustered Residential Zone
fields: Detached houses in a cluster (usually a strata), each with a possible secondary suite: up to 25 homes per hectare.
0.4 ha (about 1 acre), at least 25 m wide and 30 m deep.
Lot coverage 50%. Up to 8.5 m (about 28 ft).

zones.name: Low Density Multi-Unit Residential Zone
fields: Duplexes and townhouses: up to 40 homes per hectare.
1,200 m² (about 12,920 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.75. Lot coverage 50%. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Medium Density Multi-Unit Zone
fields: Duplexes and townhouses: up to 50 homes per hectare.
1,200 m² (about 12,920 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.

zones.name: Low Density Multi-Unit Secondary Suite Zone
fields: Duplexes and townhouses, up to 40 homes per hectare. A townhouse may have its own suite of up to 90 m².
1,200 m² (about 12,920 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.
Floor area ratio 0.75. Lot coverage 50%. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Low Rise Apartment Zone
fields: Apartments, assisted or independent living, and boarding houses. Up to 155 apartments per hectare, 225 with small units, and up to 400 with density benefits.
1,000 m² (about 10,760 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.

zones.name: Mid Rise Apartment Zone
fields: Apartments, assisted or independent living, and boarding houses. Up to 200 apartments per hectare, 250 with small units, and up to 400 with density benefits.
1,000 m² (about 10,760 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.

zones.name: Special Service Residential Zone
fields: Apartments and townhouses, with general commercial uses: up to 100 apartments per hectare.
900 m² (about 9,690 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.
Lot coverage 60%. Up to 15 m (about 49 ft).

zones.name: Supportive Housing Zone
fields: Supportive housing, up to 250 units per hectare, with sleeping units, a school and general commercial uses.
450 m² (about 4,840 sq ft), at least 15 m wide and 30 m deep.
Lot coverage 60%. Up to 15 m (about 49 ft).

zones.name: Affordable Rental Housing Zone
fields: Rental apartments, up to 365 per hectare, with a club or lodge, a school and general commercial uses.
1,000 m² (about 10,760 sq ft), at least 30 m wide and 30 m deep.
Lot coverage 60% (90% for a parking structure). Up to 25 m (about 82 ft).

zones.name: Manufactured Home Park Zone
fields: A manufactured home park. Site sizes and layout follow the city's Mobile Home Parks Bylaw.
2 ha (about 4.9 acres), at least 25 m wide.

zones.name: Commercial Conversion Zone
fields: A detached house with a secondary suite, or the house converted to a general commercial use.
450 m² (about 4,840 sq ft), at least 15 m wide and 30 m deep.
Lot coverage 50%. Up to 10 m (about 33 ft).

zones.name: Small Holding Agricultural Zone
fields: Agricultural, forest resource, commercial cannabis production, single detached residential. Commercial kennel only on lots of 4.0 ha or more.
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Upland Agricultural Zone
fields: Agricultural and forest resource uses, single detached residential; also limited outdoor paintball or laser tag.
If the lot is in the ALR, Agricultural Land Commission rules on homes, fill and subdivision also apply.

zones.name: Extensive Agricultural Zone
fields: Extensive agricultural and forest resource uses.

zones.name: Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing District
fields: R1 covers almost all of Burnaby's former single- and two-family lots. Up to 3 units on lots of 280 m² (3,014 sq ft) or less, 4 on larger lots, and 6 on lots of 281 m² or more within a Frequent Transit Network Area (400 m of a 15-minute bus stop). Forms include a house with a suite and a laneway home, duplexes, multiplexes of 3 to 6 units, cottage courts and fee-simple rowhouses. Units can be stratified; suites cannot.
281 m² and 10 m wide. Rowhouse lots: up to 280 m², 5 m wide (6.2 m for an end unit).
Front buildings up to 10 m: 2.5 storeys for 1 or 2 units, 3 storeys for 3 to 6. Rear buildings 7.5 m and 2 storeys. Basements count as a storey; flat roofs 0.5 m less.

No floor area limit. Lot coverage 40% for 1 to 4 units (30% on lots over 567 m² with 1 or 2 units), 45% for 5 or 6, and 55% on rowhouse lots. Parking: none within a Frequent Transit Network Area; elsewhere 1 space for the first unit and 0.5 for each extra unit.

zones.name: Townhouse District
fields: Live-work units, congregate housing, child care (up to 25 children) and small secondary shops and services. Home-based business, lock-off units and short-term rental.

No floor area ratio, lot size or lot coverage limits: height, setbacks, building separation and floorplate size set what can be built. At least 30% of the site permeable. Each district has an "r" sub-district for purpose-built rental.

zones.name: Low-Rise Apartment 1 District

Townhouses, live-work units, congregate housing (group homes, assisted living, care facilities), child care, and small secondary shops, cafés and services (up to 250 m² each). Home-based business, lock-off units and short-term rental as accessory uses.
Up to 4 storeys, or 6 where non-market rental housing is provided.

No floor area ratio, lot size or lot coverage limits: height, setbacks, building separation and floorplate size set what can be built. At least 30% of the site permeable. Each district has an "r" sub-district for purpose-built rental.

zones.name: Low-Rise Apartment 2 District
fields: Apartments, which may include ground-level townhouses.

Townhouses, live-work units, congregate housing (group homes, assisted living, care facilities), child care, and small secondary shops, cafés and services (up to 250 m² each). Home-based business, lock-off units and short-term rental as accessory uses.

No floor area ratio, lot size or lot coverage limits: height, setbacks, building separation and floorplate size set what can be built. At least 30% of the site permeable. Each district has an "r" sub-district for purpose-built rental.

With a residential (R) overlay on the same site, homes above or beside the commercial space, with the R district setting the height.
Pedestrian-oriented buildings up to 4 storeys. No lot size, lot coverage or floor area ratio limits; at least 20% of the site permeable.

zones.name: Residential Inclusive District
fields: R1-1 is the City of Vancouver's Residential Inclusive zone for small-scale housing. A lot of 306 m² (about 3,294 sq ft) or more can have a multiplex of 3 or 4 homes, a duplex or a single detached house. A lot of 464 m² or more can have 5 homes, and a lot of 557 m² (about 5,996 sq ft) or more can have 6, or up to 8 where all but one are rental.
A laneway house and secondary suites are conditional uses, and a character house can be kept and converted or joined by an infill home.
306 m² with 7.3 m (24 ft) of frontage for a house or duplex, and 10 m for a 3 or 4 unit multiplex; 464 m² and 13.4 m for 5 units; 557 m² and 15.1 m for 6 or more.

Floor space ratio 1.00 for a multiplex, 0.70 for a duplex and 0.60 for a single detached house. Buildings up to 11.5 m (about 38 ft) and 3 storeys; a rear building up to 8.5 m and 2 storeys. Site coverage 50% for houses and duplexes.

fields: Low-rise apartments and mixed-use residential buildings, plus apartments combined with townhouses. Smaller forms are still allowed: townhouses, duplexes, single detached houses and multiple dwellings of up to 8 units. R3-2 requires all homes to be rental.

Floor space ratio up to 2.70 for rental apartments, depending on the size and shape of the site, and up to 3.00 with 20% below-market rental in a transit-oriented area or all social housing; 2.00 or less for strata apartments in R3-1; 1.45 for other uses. zones.name: Mid-Rise Residential District (R4-1)
fields: Mid-rise apartments and mixed-use residential buildings, which must include 20% below-market rental homes or be all social housing. Low-rise apartments are also allowed. Smaller forms are still allowed: townhouses, duplexes, single detached houses and multiple dwellings of up to 8 units.
1,532 m² (about 0.38 acres) with 45.7 m of frontage, or 1,348 m² and 40 m on a corner.
Floor space ratio 4.00 for a mid-rise apartment, 4.30 for mid-rise mixed use and 1.45 for other uses. Mid-rise buildings up to 47 m (about 154 ft); low-rise 23 m, or 27.5 m with conditions.

zones.name: High-Rise Residential Districts (R5-1 to R5-4)

1,532 m² (about 0.38 acres) with 45.7 m of frontage, or 1,348 m² and 40 m on a corner.

Each RT district has its own schedule with its floor space ratio, height and character-retention rules. Check the schedule for the exact district, for example RT-7 or RT-8.

fields: The RM districts allow apartments and other multiple dwellings, with townhouses and rowhouses in several districts. Single detached houses and duplexes remain allowed in most. RM-11, RM-11N and RM-12N also list secondary suites and laneway houses.
Each RM district has its own schedule with its floor space ratio and height. Check the schedule for the exact district, for example RM-4 or RM-8A.

In C-2, multiple dwellings are a listed use and mixed-use residential buildings are conditional.

zones.name: Industrial Districts (I, IC, M and MC)
fields: Vancouver's industrial districts: I-1, I-1A, I-1B, I-1C, I-2, I-3 and I-4, IC-1 to IC-3, M-1, M-1A, M-1B and M-2, and MC-1 and MC-2. Each has its own schedule. Housing is not a general use; I-2 lists only a dwelling tied to an artist studio in certain areas.

zones.name: Historic Area Districts (HA-1 to HA-3)
fields: The historic area districts: HA-1 and HA-1A in Chinatown, HA-2 in Gastown and HA-3 in Yaletown. Each has its own schedule and design rules.

zones.name: Comprehensive Development Districts
fields: Site-specific and area-specific districts: CD-1 (each numbered CD-1 has its own by-law for one site), the Downtown District (DD), Downtown-Eastside/Oppenheimer (DEOD), False Creek (FCCDD), First Shaughnessy (FSD), Central Waterfront (CWD) and BC Place/Expo (BCPED). Check the by-law or official development plan for the property.

paras: The Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) is provincial. On ALR land, Agricultural Land Commission (ALC) rules apply in addition to municipal zoning, and local governments can add further restrictions.
Generally one residence is allowed per parcel. The principal residence can be up to 500 m² in total floor area, with no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction.
A secondary suite is allowed only inside the principal residence, and only if local bylaws allow it.

One additional detached residence may be allowed without an ALC application if only one residence exists when construction starts: up to 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or up to 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha. It does not need to be for farm help. Local zoning may still limit it.
Most subdivision of ALR land needs ALC approval, including parcels under 2 acres.

d.t: Don't assume a property can be subdivided. Check the minimum lot size, and on ALR land, ALC approval.
Zoning and ALC rules both limit homes, suites and coach houses.
Ask for septic records and have the system inspected. Septic rules come from the health authority.
Find out whether it's a well or municipal water. For a well, ask about yield, water quality and any water licence.
Ask BC Assessment whether the property has farm class. If you plan to keep livestock or poultry, ask about BC's Premises ID program.

disclaimer: This directory is a general summary prepared from each municipality's published zoning bylaw and the Agricultural Land Commission's website, checked October 2, 2026 and expanded November 18, 2026. Bylaws are amended often, site-specific zones and covenants may apply, and summaries leave out many regulations (setbacks, density, parking, floodplain and development permit requirements, among others). It is not legal, planning or survey advice. Always confirm zoning, permitted uses, lot size and ALR status directly with the municipality and the ALC before you buy, sell or build.
